Changelog

snbr 0.2.1

  • Bug fix: sn_bias() assigned wrong/NA parameter names (e.g. sigma, alpha, NA, NA) whenever the model matrix had no column names, because it indexed a too-short name vector with seq_along(). sn_info() and the matrix interface of sn_mle(), sn_br() and snplm() had the milder version of the same bug (silently unnamed output instead of wrong names). Also fixed: cbind(1, d, d^2) sets colnames() to c("", "d", ""), not NULL (R auto-names columns built from a bare symbol and leaves literal/expression columns blank), which defeated the previous is.null(colnames(X)) fallback checks. All five sites now go through a single internal helper (.coef_names(), R/utils.R) that fills in beta1, beta2, … at every missing or blank position. No numeric result changes: verified against analises/R/01_verifica_formula_artigo.R and R/13_aplicacao_lago.R, which reproduce the same values as before, now with correct labels.
  • print()/summary() on an "snbr" object now explain, when the maximum likelihood estimate of the shape is infinite, that this is an exact result rather than a numerical failure, and suggest refitting with method = "mean" or "median".

snbr 0.2.0

  • Version that accompanies the manuscript submitted to Information and Inference; every result in the manuscript and its supplement was produced with this version by the scripts in analises/R.
  • sn_br() reports why an adjusted score has no root (failure): a sign change only across alpha = 0, no sign change, or nonconvergence.
  • inst/CITATION and documentation updated to the submitted manuscript.

snbr 0.1.0

  • First version: maximum likelihood with exact detection of infinite shape estimates, Cox and Snell bias, corrective estimator, mean and median bias-reducing adjusted scores, parametric bootstrap correction, and a partially linear model with a P-spline term.
